newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac honours French vets of Spanish Civil War.
newsitem.headline: Chirac honours French vets of Spanish Civil War.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac has decided to honour the last French veterans of the International Brigades who fought on the Republican side in the 1936-1939 Spanish Civil War, the group's association said on Wednesday.

Retired Colonel Henri Rol-Tanguy, best known of the last 80 French survivors of the Brigades, got a letter from Chirac this week saying an urgent move was under way to have their efforts in Spain recognised as service to France, the group said.

France, which discreetly aided the Republicans against the insurgent right-wing nationalists led by General Francisco Franco, who went on to rule Spain until his death in 1975, officially stayed out of the fighting.

Chirac said in his letter he wanted the move completed by November 23 when French writer and long-time cultural affairs minister Andre Malraux, who led an international air squadron in the Spanish War, is reinterred in Paris' Pantheon of national heroes.

The veterans, who this month marked the 60th anniversary of the creation of the Brigades, had long campaigned for recognition as "anciens combattants" (war veterans) on grounds they were pioneers in the fight against fascism before France itself was occupied by Nazi Germany in 1940.
The move is largely symbolic because most of those involved already have veteran status and small pensions for later service in World War Two.
Some 35,000 men and women from 53 countries fought in the International Brigades, suffering 10,000 dead and earning a place in the pantheon of left-wing heroes.
The French were the single largest national contingent, supplying 9,000 volunteers of whom about a third were killed in Spain with an equal number later dying during World War Two.
While half the volunteers were non-communists, the Brigades' leadership was overwhelmingly communist.
Rol-Tanguy said earlier this month a gathering of survivors from around the world was planned for the months ahead in Madrid.
